records.name: Centro
records.current_summary: Centro contains two of Italy's six highest-victim regions for anti-LGBT violence (Lazio, Toscana per the Progetto Gionata 2012-2025 region-by-region study) and saw an activist assaulted at the Piceno Pride march in Ascoli Piceno (June 2025) with his flag seized and destroyed. Rome Pride was also targeted politically in the same June 2025 wave (the Naples Pride was attacked in the same wave but sits in Sud). The unit also contains the strongest positive institutional response found anywhere in Italy: a January 2025 Bologna first-instance conviction that recognised a "transphobic motive" behind a punitive rape of a trans sex worker, awarded damages, and - for the first time - admitted the Movimento Identita Trans as civil party. This is a judicial signal that transphobic violence is prosecuted as a distinct aggravating factor, and it applies to visitors who would rely on the same courts.  Net deviation: +0.02 above the national score (0.50). The high-victim data for Lazio and Toscana are concerning but are offset by the Bologna precedent and the absence of any criminalisation, facility ban, or enforcement mechanism targeting a visitor. The Ascoli Piceno incident is a single event with no patterned institutional failure. Compared to Nord-Ovest (0.47), Centro trades lower violence-concentration (no Alessandria killing or Brianza Roman-salute episode) for a stronger judicial response; compared to Sud (0.44), Centro lacks the railway-station public-exposure incidents and the ILGA-Europe "geographic spread" finding.

sources.claim: Dire news-agency report (24 Jan 2025): a Bologna first-instance court recognised a "transphobic motive" in the punitive rape of a trans sex worker, sentenced the perpetrator, awarded damages to the victim and to the trans-movement association that helps sex workers, and for the first time admitted the Movimento Identita Trans (MIT) as civil party - the strongest judicial recognition of transphobic aggravation recorded in this country.

Progetto Gionata region-by-region study of anti-LGBT hate-motivated violence 2012-2025: names the Italian regions with the highest victim counts, six of them ranking at the top; Lazio and Toscana (both inside Centro) are two of the six highest-victim regions, alongside Lombardia, Piemonte (Nord-Ovest), Campania and Puglia (Sud). Provides the per-region violence distribution used to score all Italian units.

records.name: Nord-Ovest
records.current_summary: Nord-Ovest bundles Italy's two most protective municipal measures for transgender people with two of the six highest-victim regions in the Progetto Gionata dataset. Milano operates Italy's first "registro di genere" (chosen name on civic documents, transport subscriptions, staff badges) and Torino runs "Identita Alias" at the comune and public libraries - practical tools that determine whether a gender-nonconforming visitor is humiliated at a ticket window or not. Against this, Lombardy and Piedmont are named as high-violence regions; a 28-year-old trans woman was found dead in Alessandria (Oct 2025), linked to a robbery series targeting vulnerable people, and right-wing militants gave Roman salutes along the Brianza Pride route (Sept 2025).  The institutional responses are notably good: the Carabinieri scientific section produced prompt charges with wiretaps and confessions in the Alessandria killing; the Digos moved pre-emptively at Brianza Pride and "struck out at birth" the spark. Lombardy's 2015 "natural family" motion and rejection of WHO sex-ed standards are dated climate signals with no visitor-facing enforcement mechanism.  Net deviation: -0.03 from the national score (0.50). The violence concentration is real for a traveler, but the protective registries and the quality of institutional responses partially offset it. Compared to Centro (0.52), this unit lacks a landmark transphobic-motive conviction but has more practical visitor-facing protections and more documented violence. Compared to Nord-Est (0.47), the protective measures here are concrete and used, not merely symbolic motions.

sources.claim: LifeGate report: Milano city council approved the first "registro di genere" in Italy (motion by Monica Romano, the first transgender woman elected to the council, 2022), granting a chosen name on civic and municipal documents, public-transport subscriptions and staff badges; Torino introduced the analogous "Identita Alias" practice at the comune and public libraries. These are the practical, visitor-facing administrative tools named in the dossier for this unit.

Progetto Gionata region-by-region study of anti-LGBT hate-motivated violence 2012-2025: names the six Italian regions with the highest victim counts; Lombardia and Piemonte (both inside Nord-Ovest) are two of the six, alongside Lazio and Toscana (Centro), Campania and Puglia (Sud). Basis of the high-violence attribution for this unit.

records.name: Nord-Est
records.current_summary: Nord-Est's distinguishing evidence is Veneto's institutionalised hostility. In 2014 the regional council approved a motion (first signer Councillor Arianna Lazzarini, deliberation no. 92 of 14 October 2014), and the regional government followed with resolution no. 2268 of 27 November 2014 — published in the region's official bulletin (BUR no. 119, 16 December 2014) — instituting an official "Festa della Famiglia Naturale" on the last school day before the Christmas holidays and formally rejecting the aims and content of the WHO Regional Office's *Standards for Sexuality Education in Europe*, committing to counter their adoption in Veneto schools. In July 2018 the council approved motion no. 340 (178th public session, Venice), pledging regional support for "those who fight in defence of the natural family" and natalist policies, attacking Pride events as "carnival farces".  Veneto, Venezia (2025): a gay student was stalked by three men who called themselves fascists, reported in the same press coverage that carried the Catania beating. No violence-monitoring data names Veneto, Trentino-Alto Adige or Friuli-Venezia Giulia among the six highest-victim regions. The special-statute regions inside this macro-region (Trentino-Alto Adige, Friuli-Venezia Giulia) have not used expanded legislative competence on gender matters. The natural-family acts and the WHO rejection are official acts of hostility and a clear climate signal to a visitor, but they do not criminalise, fine, or create enforcement exposure; the practical visitor risk from the policy layer is being unwelcome, not arrested.

sources.claim: LGBT association report (July 2018): on 3 July, in the 178th public session of the Veneto regional council in Venice, motion no. 340 (first signer Giovanna Negro) was approved, pledging regional support for "those who fight in defence of the natural family" and for natalist policies, attacking the Cirinnà civil-unions law and dismissing Pride marches as "carnival farces".

Official gazette record of Veneto regional-government resolution no. 2268 of 27 November 2014 (BUR no. 119, 16 December 2014): implementing the regional council's motion (deliberation no. 92 of 14 October 2014), it institutes the "Festa della Famiglia Naturale" on the last school day before the Christmas holidays and rejects the aims and content of the WHO Regional Office's Standards for Sexuality Education in Europe, committing to use every instrument available to counter its adoption in Veneto schools (assessor Elena Donazzan).

records.name: Sud
records.current_summary: Sud contains Campania and Puglia, two of the six highest-victim regions in the 2012–2025 region-by-region study of anti-LGBT violence, and multiple documented public-space incidents directly relevant to a traveller: in Scampia (Naples), March 2025, two young men on a scooter stopped, insulted and assaulted a young man with homophobic slurs — part of an international rights federation's finding of a troubling increase in the number and geographic spread of bias-motivated violence in 2024, with incidents reported almost monthly; and at the Torre Annunziata railway station (Campania), 13 October 2025, an activist and president of a local LGBT association was subjected to a verbal attack culminating in threats of stabbing by two young men — a public-transit setting any visitor could encounter. In Reggio Calabria (28 May 2024) a person was kidnapped, subjected to violence and robbed in the city centre; the police's swift intervention drew public commendation from Arcigay alongside demands for an anti-homophobia law.  Taranto (Puglia) and Termoli (Molise) featured in the 2025 national Pride circuit, indicating continued public LGBTQ presence in the south. No special-statute region in Sud used expanded competence against transgender people, and no criminal facility bans or enforcement mechanisms target visitors. The violence is criminal and street-level, not state-imposed — but its concentration and public-transit exposure raise the probability of encounter for a traveller.

records.name: Isole
records.current_summary: Isole's evidence is dominated by Sicily. In April 2025 three young men were beaten in a Catania fast-food restaurant at roughly 5 a.m. solely because they were gay; the victims were hospitalised, video of the attack later circulated publicly, and the prosecutor's office reconstructed the sequence (insults and threats, then the physical assault). In July 2025 a mother was attacked in Catania in an incident named in a national statement accusing the national government of "exposing us to violence". A June 2026 survey of Sicilian reporting describes a sustained pattern of rising homophobic bullying, violence against the LGBTQIA+ community and associated suicides, listing multiple cases — a patterned finding, not a single incident. Favignana (Trapani) has also hosted a national Pride-circuit march, showing visibility persists alongside the harm. No Sardinia-specific evidence was found.  Sicily is not among the six highest-victim regions in the quantitative study, but the qualitative pattern — multiple cases, suicides, a hospitalisation-level assault in a tourist-accessible city — indicates a severity profile that elevates real risk for a visitor in nightlife and public-street settings. Neither special-statute island (Sicilia, Sardegna) has used expanded legislative competence against transgender people. The violence is criminal, not state-enforced.

sources.claim: National TV news chronicle (August 2025): the Catania fast-food homophobic beating of three gay men on 26 April 2025 — victims hospitalised; the reconstruction of insults, threats and the assault from circulated video, and the prosecutors' sequence, are set out case by case.

Regional news survey (June 2026) of homophobia in Sicily: lists multiple cases of rising homophobic bullying, violence against LGBTQIA+ people and associated suicides across the island — the sustained-pattern finding for the region.

records.name: Alberta
records.current_summary: Alberta is the only jurisdiction in the country to pass laws targeting transgender people as a class and then shield those laws from judicial review. Three bills, announced in January 2024 and enacted in December 2024: the Education Amendment Act 2024 requires parental notification/consent before staff use a student's gender-related preferred name or pronouns (in full force since 1 September 2025); the Health Statutes Amendment Act 2024 prohibits puberty blockers and hormone therapy for minors; and a vital-statistics rule was amended. A 2025 government bill invoked the constitutional notwithstanding clause over all three laws, and after it passed, a Court of King's Bench judge lifted the injunction that had been pausing the care ban; a government appeal succeeded, removing the injunction. Two national 2SLGBTQ+ organisations, with five gender-diverse youth, continue a constitutional challenge despite the shield ("the fight isn't over").  These school and healthcare provisions are primarily resident-facing and carry small traveler-facing weight. The more directly relevant signal is the documented street-level pattern in Calgary: from 2023 a pastor led repeated disruptions of library drag-storytime events — charging into a library classroom and shouting homophobic and transphobic slurs at parents and children, who left crying — and the litigation has run for years: a conviction for harassing a librarian was upheld on appeal, acquittals on disturbance and mischief charges were overturned with a new trial ordered, and a further breach conviction followed in 2026. Reporting from March 2023 noted many drag events cancelled or postponed in Calgary as threats and protests escalated. The pairing of trans-targeting legislation, a judicial-override shield and a documented event-cancellation pattern marks a clear hardening of provincial posture.

sources.claim: National public broadcaster (4 December 2024): the trio of Alberta bills affecting transgender people — pronoun/parental-notification opt-ins in schools, the ban on gender-affirming care for minors, and a vital-statistics change — passed the legislature's final stage; 2SLGBTQ+ advocacy groups say they will continue legal action.

National public broadcaster (December 2025): Bill 9 invoked the notwithstanding clause to shield the three transgender-affecting laws from legal action; Egale Canada and Skipping Stone, with five gender-diverse youth, say they will continue the court challenge of the care-ban law regardless ("the fight isn't over").

records.name: Saskatchewan
records.current_summary: Saskatchewan's provincial government enacted a parental-consent rule for students under 16 (name/pronoun policy, Aug 2023), which the Court of King's Bench struck down in UR Pride Centre for Sexuality and Gender Diversity v Saskatchewan, 2023 SKKB 204. The government responded by legislating the rule into the Education Act (s.197.4, The Education (Parents' Bill of Rights) Amendment Act, 2023) and invoking Charter s.33 to immunise it from judicial review. The matter returned to the Court of Appeal as Saskatchewan (Minister of Education) v UR Pride Centre, 2025 SKCA 74 (11 Aug 2025).  The school policy is resident-facing and carries small traveler-facing weight. The significant signal is the government's pattern of overriding a court that found the law unconstitutional — a structural escalation in provincial posture toward trans people that a visitor would register as hostile climate (provincial statements, board-meeting activity, protest presence). No documented street-level disruption or cancellation of public events was found in the dossier. The 2021 gender-related homicide rate (1.03 per 100k, highest provincial) is a weak, non-trans-specific proxy.  Deviation: 0.07 below the national score of 0.86. The notwithstanding clause use places Saskatchewan clearly below provinces without legislative hostility, but the absence of a documented traveler-facing incident series (unlike Alberta's Calgary pattern) limits the gap. Compared to Alberta (0.76), Saskatchewan scores higher because the legislative weapon is identical but the street-level cancellation pattern is absent. Compared to British Columbia (0.82), Saskatchewan is lower because BC had disruptions but no provincial override of courts.

sources.claim: Government of Saskatchewan education-ministry news release (22 Aug 2023) announcing the parental inclusion and consent policies: schools must seek parent/guardian permission before changing the preferred name and pronouns of students under 16, parents must be informed about the sexual-health curriculum, and third-party school programs were paused. The release that started the court challenge.

records.name: Scotland
records.current_summary: Scotland diverges from the UK baseline in one live, visitor-relevant direction: the Hate Crime and Public Order (Scotland) Act 2021 (in force 1 April 2024) created the UK's only dedicated transgender-identity hate-crime aggravation. COPFS reported 104 charges carrying that aggravation in 2025-26 (up 21% on 86 the year before), and Police Scotland recorded 8,538 hate crimes in 2024-25 — the first full year of the Act. Anti-trans offending in Scotland is therefore named in charging as a distinct statutory category; in England and Wales, transgender identity appears in police recording as one of the five monitored strands, but no equivalent transgender charging aggravation exists. For an assaulted or harassed visitor that is the difference between a crime the prosecution system is built to identify by name and one it is not. The wider climate corroborates the law: Holyrood passed expansive gender-recognition reform by a two-thirds majority, and Scottish public opinion on LGBT equality runs consistently ahead of the UK average (British Social Attitudes).  What does  not  count against Scotland as local hostility: the Section 35 veto of that reform and the June 2026 Court of Session ruling voiding the Scottish Prison Service's trans custody guidance were both applications of UK-wide law and the UK Supreme Court's biological-sex definition — the same mechanisms visitors face in every British nation, already priced into the national score (0.48). They erased Scotland's attempt to rise  above  that baseline; they did not push it below. Scotland therefore scores above the national anchor: the charging machinery plus the most trans-accepting electorate and government in the Isles. Vs Wales (≈0.51): inclusive posture, no charging aggravation. Vs England: recording strand without a charging aggravation; vs Northern Ireland (0.42): withdrawn school guidance, stalled hate-crime inclusion.

Direct evidence that the dedicated transgender aggravation under the 2021 Act is actively used in charging decisions.

records.name: Oaxaca
records.current_summary: In May 2024, the organising brotherhood of the Vela San Vicente Ferrer 'Goola' in Juchitán circulated a written invitation stating 'men dressed as women will not be admitted.' Muxe activists including poet-lawyer Elvis Guerra filed a CONAPRED discrimination complaint, saying 'this is not the muxe paradise.' These festivals are explicitly marketed to foreign tourists, making the exclusion directly visitor-facing. The state human-rights ombudsperson opened 34 discrimination investigations involving LGBTIQ+ people between 2015 and 2022, with attacks on trans people prompting public demands for justice. April 2025 reporting characterised Oaxaca as Mexico's fastest-growing tourist paradise but 'the most dangerous state for the LGBT+ community,' with several violent incidents under investigation for possible municipal-police participation in regions where armed groups operate; authorities responded by stepping up visitor security.  Countervailing: legal gender recognition since 2019, extended to age 12+ in 2021 and fully opened by a 2023 Supreme Court ruling; traditional muxe recognition is culturally real (the 'Auténticas Intrépidas Buscadoras del Peligro' vela held its 49th annual edition). The positive and negative signals coexist: the formal legal framework is protective, but customary-exclusion enforcement at the exact events tourists attend creates a specific travel risk.  Context for comparison: Yucatán, with no dedicated incident record, has marched Pride for 23 consecutive editions (to June 2025) with no ban and no counter-attack reported in 2024-25; Mexico City meets comparable lethality with a dedicated transfeminicide investigation unit and mandatory-response protocols. In Oaxaca the violence is attributed partly to police participation and answered with visitor-security steps rather than structural reform.

The exclusion comes from traditional festival authorities at events marketed to foreign tourists.

Trendencias feature (April 2025): profiles Oaxaca as Mexico's fastest-growing tourist paradise that is simultaneously 'the most dangerous state for the LGBT+ community'; several violent incidents are under investigation with possible municipal-police participation, in municipalities where armed groups operate; the state's answer has been stepped-up visitor security rather than institutional reform.

El Universal (2026): the Oaxaca human-rights ombudsperson (Defensoría) opened 34 discrimination investigations involving LGBTIQ+ people between 2015 and 2022; attacks against trans people have pushed the community to publicly demand justice, and violence against muxes persists despite the state's international reputation for diversity.

Human Rights Watch feature on state gender-recognition laws in Mexico (March 2025): Oaxaca has had legal gender recognition since 2019, extended it to 12-year-olds by decree in 2021, and a 2023 Supreme Court ruling fully opened the procedure; 22 of 32 states had legislated a procedure by March 2025, while six state legislatures have enacted none at all.

records.name: Tripura
records.current_summary: Tripura exhibits the country's clearest border-checkpoint pattern of profiling gender-nonconforming presentation as a suspicion trigger for foreign infiltration. In early August 2024, police reported apprehending 15 Bangladeshi nationals including seven transgender individuals in separate incidents within 24 hours; the group intercepted at the Panisagar check post numbered seven, per police reporting two transgender individuals plus others "disguised as third-gender" — the framing that trans presentation is a disguise for infiltration is explicit in the police account. In November 2024, coordinated 24-hour operations across the state detained twelve more Bangladeshi nationals, including minors and transgender people. The state shares an 856 km border with Bangladesh. These are named-state-actor operations with published counts, constituting a patterned enforcement practice directly facing any trans-presenting visitor crossing by land.  The deviation from the national 0.43 is substantial (−0.12): while India has no statute criminalising trans presence, Tripura's checkpoint regime converts gender-nonconforming appearance into an independently sufficient reason for detention and deportation proceedings. Compared to West Bengal (0.34), which shares the same script but records it in fewer, more isolated incidents, Tripura's repeated 24-hour sweep operations and the explicit "disguise" framing make it the most concentrated instance of this visitor-facing harm in the country.  Tripura does have a constituted transgender welfare board (one of only 12 states/UTs), but the RTI investigation found most such boards to be "rudderless" with no compliance mechanism or real power — this institutional presence does not offset active police profiling at the border.

sources.claim: Sentinel Assam report (2 Aug 2024): in the past 24 hours Tripura authorities apprehended 15 Bangladeshi nationals including seven transgender individuals in separate incidents; the first involved a bus intercepted at the Panisagar check post (North Tripura district), detainees carrying fake Aadhaar and PAN cards; state shares an 856-km porous border. Primary count for the August sweep.

Northeast Today report (2 Aug 2024): seven Bangladeshi nationals apprehended at the Panisagar check post on the Agartala highway en route to Mumbai — per the article, two transgender individuals plus others police described as "disguised as third-gender" persons. The source of the explicit disguise framing.

Sentinel Assam report (9 Nov 2024): in coordinated operations across Tripura over 24 hours, twelve Bangladeshi nationals including minors and transgender people were detained; a post-midnight group of six included three transgender persons, destined for Mumbai. Establishes the pattern recurring months after the August cluster.

Press Information Bureau, Government of India (8 Dec 2021, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment): state-wise list of the 12 states/UTs that had constituted Transgender Welfare Boards under section 10(1) of the Transgender Persons Rules 2020 — Tripura included. Official record of the board's existence.

The Quint RTI investigation (5 Nov 2024) into state Transgender Welfare Boards: most of the 12 constituted boards lack a compliance mechanism or real power and were found leaderless or inactive — the basis for treating board existence as nominal rather than an offset to border profiling.
